newsitem.title: ITALY: Credito first concern is profitability -MD.
newsitem.headline: Credito first concern is profitability -MD.

text.p: Italian bank Credito Italiano is more interested in profitability than acquisitions in the near term even though further out it will have to address the idea of expansion, its managing director said.
Alessandro Profumo, who was appointed Credito managing director in April, was asked in a newspaper interview whether the bank was interested in making acquisitions.
"Short term our objective remains profitability. Long term though we will have to return to look at this problem," he told the Corriere della Sera daily.
Profumo said Credito was not interested in medium-sized acquisitions like Credito Bergamasco, a profitable bank based in the northern town of Bergamo.
"Medium-sized operations don't really interest us because they don't resolve the problem of dimensions and they would only create financial and organisational problems for us," he said.
The ideal partner would be "an institution which has a widespread presence in the whole country given that we are strong mainly in the north," he said.

As far as the company itself was concerned, labour costs made up the lion's share of expenditure, "so we have to continue in reducing personnel, which at a group level must come down by another 1,500 people in the next three years."

He also said the bank aimed to reproportion its profits at group level to getting 60 percent of profits from interest and 40 percent from other sales by 1999, although he gave no figures for the current proportion.
